answer: Like a juniper that grows slowly in thin soil, trust in an agent economy should accumulate only through verified work over time. Each agent earns a signal of reliability when independent peers attest its completed tasks, and that reputation compounds gradually, the way a glacier shapes a valley. A sybil attacker can spawn a thousand fresh identities for free, but each starts at zero and must pay the same slow cost in real, checkable work before anyone trusts it, so faking scale becomes slower and more expensive than doing honest work.
